title: Evidence Outline
description: Condensed exam outline of Classes 1–19 on the Fall 2026 syllabus (Fisher pp. 1–783). Part I covers the Federal Rules, jury secrecy under 606(b), relevance, conditional relevance, and 403. Part II covers the specialized relevance rules, 407–411. Part III covers character evidence: the propensity ban, 404(b), Huddleston, 413–415, the defendant's and victim's character, and habit. Part IV covers impeachment under 607–609 and the rape shield. Part V covers competency, the definition of hearsay, opposing parties' statements, prior statements of witnesses, and the 803, 804, and 807 exceptions. Part VI covers the Confrontation Clause from Crawford through Smith v. Arizona. Part VII covers completeness, Bruton, and Chambers. Part VIII covers lay and expert opinion from the Week 10 reading. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every principal case with its class.

Tier 2 gets 64: tender, inspection, acceptance and payment, course of performance and waiver, modification, quantity and price, the parol evidence rule, assignment and delegation, insecurity and repudiation, excuse, and remedy limits. Tier 3 gets 20: scope, formation and § 2-207, the statute of frauds, good faith and variation by agreement, and termination. Each exam has 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions in Professor Richardson's sample-exam format, mixing short hypos that ask who wins and why with "Which of the following is NOT…" questions. Wrong answers are built from the near-miss rules she tests, and some questions offer "None of the above," which is sometimes the answer. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or topic, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.

title: Sales and Leases Complete Coverage Exams
description: 31 quick-fire practice exams (465 new questions) that together test every rule and concept from Weeks 1–8. A checklist of 446 rules and concepts, built from every slide in the Week 1 through Week 8 decks, the Sepinuck casebook (cases, notes and assigned problems) and the statutory supplement (UCC text and Official Comments), was used to write them, and every item on it is tested at least once. The questions are short: one- or two-line rule questions and mini-hypos, many of them "Which of the following is NOT…" questions that test four or five rules at once. Each exam has 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions in Professor Richardson's sample-exam format and samples the whole course, from which law governs and the battle of the forms through warranties, risk of loss, disclaimers, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment, repudiation and excuse. Wrong answers are the near misses: the common-law rule the UCC changed, the wrong number or section, merchant vs. non-merchant, the rule from the next section over. Some questions offer "None of the above" or "All of the above," and sometimes that is the answer. The 23 questions that change the facts of another question ("Same contract, but…") name the question they build on and show its facts, so shuffling or filtering never leaves you without them. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or by any of 24 topic areas, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.

title: Civil Procedure Outline

Part III covers notice and service. Part IV covers subject-matter jurisdiction: federal question, diversity and alienage, supplemental jurisdiction, and removal. Part V covers venue, transfer, forum-selection clauses, and forum non conveniens. Part VI covers the Erie doctrine. Part VII covers pleading, Rule 11, and responding to the complaint. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every assigned case (29 main cases) plus slide references and supplemental readings.
